description: Hidden Phase-1 case used Phase-2 syntax (BETWEEN); conforming Phase-1 engines answer UNSUPPORTED.
impact: Validation verdict only (hidden test); runs re-validated, earlier verdict kept in validation-history/.
prevention: spec_validate lints Phase-1 cases for Phase-2 syntax.

description: Runner overwrote explicit ids of request steps with its step counter, so the two id-echo cases in phase1/limits_and_output.pqt failed for every engine.
impact: Agents saw 2 spurious public failures during development (possible wasted effort; inspect transcripts before attributing effort metrics). Validation verdicts re-computed.

description: Validation used the workspace copy of tests/ and spec/, which an agent could modify.
impact: None observed: no workspace modified tests/, spec/, datasets/ or tools/ (verified with git diff against the baseline commit).

description: Java and Go agents independently noted that comparing an INT64 beyond 18 digits with a DECIMAL raises NUMERIC_OVERFLOW under the literal promotion rule. Candidate clarification via change control after the wave.

Fuzzer required an error for 'SELECT 1+1+...+1' (20001 terms), which is valid SQL with no spec size limit (correct answer 20001). Go, Java, Clojure and Common Lisp were correct and were reported as 1 problem each.
impact: Robustness results only (fuzz is not part of acceptance). Fixed: such inputs must yield the correct result or a clean non-INTERNAL error; setup load is asserted; succeeded responses are counted.

description: The spec has no implementation limits for expression size/nesting. Rust answers a 20001-term expression with PARSE_ERROR (others compute it). Candidate change: allow RESOURCE_LIMIT for exceeding documented implementation limits, require a minimum supported depth (e.g. 1000).

Hand-written CR-1 case (line 51, not oracle-checked) expected DECIMAL(18,2) for INT64 UNION ALL orders.amount, but the case loaded orders.csv without a schema; inference never yields DECIMAL, so amount is FLOAT64 and FLOAT64 is the correct answer. Go, Python and Rust all returned FLOAT64 and were classified tests_failed.
impact: Spurious public failure visible to every change-union-all agent; affected runs re-validated with the fixed case, earlier verdicts kept in validation-history/.
prevention: Hand-written expectations get an explicit schema for DECIMAL columns; run new change cases against at least one engine (expected failures only on the new capability) before launching a wave.
